parts.latex: By calculating a $z$-score, find the percentage of scores that are between 58 and 70.
parts.note: Normal probability read from a z-table, which is not in the 2024 course (only the empirical rule).

parts.latex: Explain why the percentage of scores between 46 and 70 is twice your answer to part (a).
By using the values in the table above, find an approximate minimum score that a candidate would need to be placed in the top $10\%$ of the candidates.
parts.note: Top 10% score found from a z-table of normal probabilities, which is not in the 2024 course.

solutions.latex:
Find the $z$-score of $70$, using $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ with $\mu=58$ and $\sigma=15$:
$$\begin{aligned} z &= \dfrac{70-58}{15} \\ &= 0.8 \end{aligned}$$
From the table, $P(Z<0.8)=0.7881$. The mean $58$ has $z=0$, with $P(Z<0)=0.5$.
$$\begin{aligned} P(58<X<70) &= 0.7881-0.5 \\ &= 0.2881 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{about } 28.8\% \text{ of scores lie between } 58 \text{ and } 70$$

meta.self_check: Standard normal value P(Z<0.8)=0.7881 checked; the table itself was not visible.
meta.generated_note: Generated worked solution; table value for z = 0.8 assumed to be 0.7881 (standard normal).

solutions.latex:
The score $46$ is $12$ below the mean, since $58-46=12$. The score $70$ is $12$ above the mean, since $70-58=12$.

The normal distribution is symmetric about the mean $58$, so the proportion of scores between $46$ and $58$ equals the proportion between $58$ and $70$.

$$\therefore\ \text{the percentage between } 46 \text{ and } 70 \text{ is twice the answer to part (a)}$$

The top $10\%$ of candidates means $P(Z<z)=0.90$.

The table value closest to $0.90$ is $P(Z<1.3)=0.9032$, so $z\approx 1.3$.

Convert back to a score, using $x=\mu+z\sigma$:
$$\begin{aligned} x &= 58+1.3\times 15 \\ &= 77.5 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the minimum score needed is approximately } 77.5$$
